LESSON: MECHANICS OF WRITING: PUNCTUATION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Writing 3.4 Guided Writing: Sequencing Ideas (2 sessions) • Vocabulary building 
Topic 3.6: Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation, part of Writing 3.4 Guided Writing: Sequencing Ideas (2 sessions) • Vocabulary building  in Grade 7 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: Why do we go shopping? 2. How do punctuation marks contribute to meaning in texts?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work jointly to identify punctuation marks used in writing texts in the Arabic language,

2. draw the punctuation marks on charts and display them in class,

3. work jointly to match punctuation marks to their uses,

4. practise writing simple sentences on shopping for food and drinks using correct punctuation,

5. collaborate to punctuate a paragraph appropriately,

6. organise their well-punctuated paragraphs in the class portfolio. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work jointly to identify punctuation marks used in writing texts in the Arabic language,
2. draw the punctuation marks on charts and display them in class,
3. work jointly to match punctuation marks to their uses,
4. practise writing simple sentences on shopping for food and drinks using correct punctuation,
5. collaborate to punctuate a paragraph appropriately,
6. organise their well-punctuated paragraphs in the class portfolio. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and Problem-solving: This is developed as the learner analyses concepts keenly to identify how best to

punctuate a paragraph.

• Learning to Learn: This is nurtured as the learner builds on their learning experiences through a self-directed assessment

when organising their well-punctuated paragraphs in the class portfolio.
